name: Knockaulin

site of recent Celtic earthwork excavations
often confused with the Hill of Allen

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Knockaulin is an Irish mythological place. It was once the royal seat of the kings of Leinster. Their province lay in the east of Ireland. The original name was Dun Ailinne. Its standing equaled Tara in Mide and the Ulster stronghold of Macha. The hill now carries earthworks that recent digs uncovered. That work backs local claims about the site. The low hill rests near Kilcullen in County Kildare. People often confuse it with the Allen hill close at hand. That hill holds the seat of the hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill.
